newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end firmer after late selling.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end firmer after late selling.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly higher on Monday after poor trade statistics released by the government wiped out much of early gains, brokers said.
The composite index ended 1.35 points higher at a provisional 727.83.
Rumours that the finance ministry would urge state-managed funds to increase stock buying buoyed sentiment towards the morning close. Ministry officials denied the speculation.
But share prices began sliding after the trade ministry announced the country's trade deficit widened to $1.83 billion in November from $414 million a year earlier, brokers said.
"The market is likely to move narrowly tomorrow in the absence of fresh factors," said Yoo Jae-kyong, a broker at Daishin Securities.
Trade volume totalled 23.47 million shares, compared with 14.15 million for Saturday's half-day trading. Gainers outpaced losers by 511 to 358 with 153 remaining unchanged.
Brokers said expectations of fewer stock supplies in December also boosted overall sentiment.
They estimated this month's stock supplies, including rights and bonus issues, at about 270 billion won, compared with 900 billion in November.
Brokers said an overhang of loans for margin trading, currently estimated at 2.75 trillion won, kept blue chips from rising.
Samsung Electronics fell 200 won to 60,100, POSCO 600 won to 40,800 and Korea Mobile Telecom 5,000 won to 445,000..
Customer deposits with securities houses stood at 2.48 trillion won against this year's high of 3.3 trillion in May.
